diagnostics.message: local_file.public_ssh_key declares an explicit depends_on on tls_private_key.ssh, but this dependency is already established implicitly by the data reference `content = tls_private_key.ssh.public_key_openssh`. The explicit depends_on is redundant and can be removed.

local_file.private_ssh_key declares an explicit depends_on on tls_private_key.ssh, but this dependency is already established implicitly by the data reference `content = tls_private_key.ssh.private_key_pem`. The explicit depends_on is redundant and can be removed.

The user-data script embedded in aws_launch_configuration.gitlab_runner_instance interacts with the SSM parameter at run time: it reads the runner token from the parameter named by local.secure_parameter_store_runner_token_key, and if absent registers the runner and writes the new token back to that parameter (the aws_ssm_parameter resource itself uses lifecycle ignore_changes for "value" for exactly this reason). No attribute reference or depends_on links the launch configuration (or the autoscaling group that launches instances from it) to aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token. If the instance boots before Terraform creates the parameter, the user-data script will create the SSM parameter out-of-band, causing Terraform's creation of the parameter to fail with "already exists" or to introduce state drift. The SSM parameter must be created before the runner instance is launched.
